I finally caved and got the app and it helped SO MUCH to find products that work for me. I have fungal acne, psoriasis, and sensitive skin. So it helped to narrow down exact products that will work for me

reviews.title: Please Try!
reviews.text:
OVERVIEW: Great app: includes ingredient breakdowns, skincare tailored towards specific concerns, and product dupes based on pricing and ingredients. 
I go through an obscene amount of sifting through product reviews to search for the perfect fit for my skin routine. On a whim, I thought I’d try a free trial of this app. I’m really bad at canceling subscriptions, but didn’t cancel and paid for the full year (there’s a subscription refund available) and decided to keep perusing SkinSort. What I’ve found is a really kind, and articulate little skincare community. Lately, I’ve been really wrapped up in building reviews as well as commenting on others’ reviews too. What I wish for this app moving forward is that reviews remain unbiased and NOT incentivized. I’ve been influenced enough and I just want honest reviews. Full disclosure: I have NOT been paid to write this. Happy skincare journey!

reviews.title: My go to when looking for a new skincare product

reviews.title: Can be misleading
reviews.text: Overall it’s a cool aggregator of information, but it can present it in a really misleading way—especially in the personalized scoring feature. As someone with extremely sensitive skin, this tool seemed initially a godsend, but when I tried using products that scored 90%+ for me, the results were horrible. My skin was burning and inflamed when using a popular product the app recommended to me. When instead I used a product that scored in the red < 50% for suitability, my skin felt much better. For laymen like me, I think it’s best to use this app just to check for ingredients, but don’t follow its advice. Save your money for a dermatologist.

reviews.title: Overpriced Search Engine
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like SkinSort, but it ended up being a disappointment. The app feels like a stripped-down search engine. It’s less useful than just looking things up on Google or even browsing Reddit, where you get a wider range of users’ experiences and opinions.

One of the biggest issues is how misleading it is about creating a “routine.” That feature is either extremely limited or just not actually functional in a meaningful way. I expected something personalized and helpful, but it didn’t deliver.

There’s also no consideration for budget when suggesting products, which makes the recommendations feel out of touch and impractical. For something that’s paid, I expected a lot more value and usability.

Overall, it feels overpriced for what it offers, and I honestly regret paying for it. I wish I could get a refund.

reviews.title: So Helpful for Screening Allergens
reviews.text:
This app has made navigating my various skin allergies so much easier because I was truly at a loss before I found it since I have several allergens that are found in…everything. Knowing what stores carry certain items and the fact that it has so much information about international brands is such a game changer!! I have never been so happy to have found an app. 

My only criticism is that it will tell you that a product in your routine doesn’t work well (based on skin goals, avoided ingredients) BUT the products it suggests are equally ill matched. Same with the option to see dupes that would work better. This is only tricky because my reason for using the app is to avoid specific ingredients.
